speaker: Dr. Alan Baratz, CEO, D-Wave Quantum Inc.

checkins.note: Flatiron Institute (Joseph Tindall et al.) posted a classical belief-propagation approach to arXiv claiming it “demonstrably outperforms other reported methods” on the same spin-glass problem, with errors “noticeably lower than the quantum annealing approach” -- not yet peer-reviewed at time of posting.
checkins.author: desk

checkins.note: Linda Mauron and Giuseppe Carleo (EPFL) posted a separate classical approach (time-dependent variational Monte Carlo) to arXiv, reporting correlation errors below 7% on systems up to 128 spins -- “aligning with or surpassing” D-Wave's reported accuracy at that scale, though not yet tested at D-Wave's largest reported instances.
checkins.author: desk

verbatim: Our demonstration of quantum computational supremacy on a useful problem is an industry first.
headline: D-Wave says its Advantage2 annealing quantum computer demonstrated quantum computational supremacy on a real-world magnetic-materials simulation problem, beating classical supercomputers.
source_kind: press release, tied to a peer-reviewed Science paper
resolution_criteria: This is a claim about a result already published (Science, DOI 10.1126/science.ado6285, “Beyond-Classical Computation in Quantum Simulation”), not a future promise -- so what is being tracked is not whether it happens, but whether it HOLDS UP against classical rebuttals, which is exactly the kind of claim a credibility tracker exists for. Resolves VERIFIED if no classical algorithm has, by the resolution date, matched D-Wave's reported accuracy/runtime on the same problem instances at the same or larger scale. NOT_VERIFIED if a peer-reviewed classical method has matched or beaten it at comparable scale. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if classical methods match it at smaller scales tested so far (as the two rebuttals below currently claim) but have not yet been shown to scale to D-Wave's largest reported instances.
resolver_sources: arXiv:2503.05693 (Flatiron Institute, Tindall, Mello, Fishman et al.)
